svg.title: The RPF source stack: five tables consulted in priority order, and the leftover static mroute that beats all of them
svg.desc: Five stacked rows in priority order. First and highest, a static mroute, which overrides the unicast path and whose danger is a legacy leftover that causes permanent silent RPF failure. Second, MBGP with SAFI 2, allowing multicast to leave by a different exit at the cost of two policy sets. Third, MTR multitopology, which fully separates multicast from unicast but requires per-topology IGP support. Fourth, the unicast RIB, the default, where any unicast change moves multicast with it. Fifth, the default route, whose danger is that a source matching only 0.0.0.0/0 may RPF out of the wrong interface. A right column gives the three typical failure causes - asymmetric unicast and multicast paths, ECMP where only one path receives, and an unreachable BGP next hop - and the three-command drill: show ip rpf, show ip mroute, show ip mroute count.
svg.text: RPF asks five tables, in order, and stops at the first match
Two independent routing policies are already a risk. Five of them stacked is why "the route is there" is not an answer.
PRIORITY 1
Static mroute
ip mroute <src> <mask> <if | nh>
Emergency override of the unicast path.
A leftover entry fails silently and forever.
PRIORITY 2
MBGP, SAFI 2
address-family ipv4 multicast
Multicast takes a different exit than unicast.
Cost: two policies to keep in step.
PRIORITY 3
MTR, multitopology
topology + ip pim binding
Full separation of the two topologies.
Cost: IGP must support per-topology metrics.
PRIORITY 4
Unicast RIB
IGP / BGP / static
The default answer, and the usual one.
Any unicast change moves multicast with it.
PRIORITY 5
Default route
Fallback when nothing else knows the source.
RPF may point out of the wrong interface.
THREE CAUSES OF FAILURE
1. Asymmetric path
Unicast prefers A, the stream arrives on B.
Fix the metric, or pin a static mroute.
2. ECMP
Two equal paths, only one receives.
ip multicast multipath hashes on the source.
3. BGP next hop unreachable
The best route is unusable for RPF.
THE THREE-COMMAND DRILL
show ip rpf 10.1.1.10
RPF interface, RPF neighbour, RPF type
show ip mroute 239.10.1.1
IFF, OIL, flags, packet counters
show ip mroute count
RPF failed counter, the only evidence
WHY THE STACK MATTERS TO A DESIGN
If you use RPF 2 or 3, write it down
Two policies mean two place to make the same
mistake, and only one of them is in the LLD.
Audit static mroutes quarterly
They outrank everything and never expire.
A forgotten one survives two migrations.
Never accept RPF 5 by accident
A source that only matches the default route
will RPF out of the WAN and work by luck.
